newsitem.title: GUYANA: Guyana upset by phone sex image.
newsitem.headline: Guyana upset by phone sex image.

text.p: Guyana criticised on Wednesday a U.S. telephone company for tarnishing its image with an international phone sex business.
Trade Minister Michael Shree Chan said the government had previously asked the firm, Atlantic Tele-Network Inc., to stop its sex call business, without luck.

The Washington Post reported on Monday that Atlantic Tele- Network could earn "nearly $100 million from its burgeoning trade in specialised information services, such as telephone sex, as dialers ... place international calls to X-rated services in Guyana."
Asked about the report, Chan told Reuters: "Guyana's name is tarnished internationally. Such a situation ought not to be allowed to continue."

He did not say what measures, if any, the Guyanese government could take against Atlantic Tele-Network, which is based in the U.S. Virgin Islands. The firm bought 80 percent of Guyana Telegraph and Telephone (GT&T) for $16.5 million in 1991.
Chan said the government -- which retained 20 percent of GT&T -- had asked it in the past to concentrate on providing house and business telephone lines to thousands of people who need them.

He deplored that the company was "primarily concerned with the maximum of profits, notwithstanding the repeated call by the Guyana government, church bodies and the consumer association for the withdrawal of the offensive audiotext services."

The Guyanese government was concerned to see GT&T departing from the stated objective of providing telephone facilities to the people of the former British colony "and making its business mainly one that provides audiotext services to customers outside Guyana," he added.
